choices.text:
The function reads a length `n` from the XDR stream and then reads `n` bytes into a destination buffer `dst`. On line 10, it attempts to null-terminate the string by writing `'\0'` at `dst[n]`.

The vulnerability is a buffer overflow (off-by-one). The code checks if `n` bytes are available in the input stream, but it does not check if the destination buffer `dst` (defined by `base + desc->offset`) has enough space to hold `n + 1` bytes. Since `n` is a `uint32_t` provided by the input stream, an attacker can provide a value of `n` that fills the allocated slice exactly, causing `dst[n]` to write a null byte outside the bounds of the allocated memory.

Answer: 10
